metadata.scope: Canadian MPs OSINT profiles — lobbying, MAID votes, controversies
metadata.methodology: Public web sources, parliamentary records, lobbying registry, news archives
metadata.disclaimer: All claims sourced from publicly available records. No fabricated information.

profiles.name: Jonathan Wilkinson
cabinet_roles: Minister of Fisheries, Oceans, and the Canadian Coast Guard (2018-2019)
Minister of Environment and Climate Change (2019-2021)
Minister of Energy and Natural Resources (2021-2025)

controversies.title: Teck Resources Conflict of Interest Complaint
controversies.summary: Democracy Watch filed a formal complaint with the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner alleging Wilkinson violated the Conflict of Interest Act through involvement in decisions related to an IJC investigation into water pollution from Teck Resources Elk Valley coal mines in BC.
details: His spouse holds investments in RBC, TD, and BlackRock Inc., all among Teck's top 25 institutional shareholders
He was CEO of BioteQ Environmental Technologies, which had a contract from Teck to treat selenium contamination in mine wastewater, before entering politics
Teck lobbied him directly on mining issues six times in the year preceding the complaint

lobbying_highlights.detail: As Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, was among the most-lobbied ministers by the fossil fuel industry

lobbying_highlights.note: 34 meetings with fossil fuel lobbyists in 2023
15 meetings with fossil fuel lobbyists in 2024, second only to Chrystia Freeland (19)
Created a 'dedicated process' to work with the Pathways Alliance (consortium of 6 major oil sands companies)
CAPP (Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers) specifically targeted Wilkinson in lobbying campaigns in 2023; 3 of his 4 May 2023 meetings were with CAPP
NRCan was the most frequently targeted ministry with 337 fossil fuel lobbying meetings in 2023

profiles.maid_position: Voted YES on both Bill C-14 (2016, legalizing MAID) and Bill C-7 (2020, expanding MAID eligibility). No public dissenting statements found; voted in line with Liberal Party position.

foreign_connections.note: No CIJA-sponsored trips to Israel found in public records
foreign_connections.detail: Independent Jewish Voices held a demonstration outside his constituency office in October 2023 calling for a Gaza ceasefire, but no direct Israel trip or foreign connection found

financial_notes.note: Spousal financial interests in RBC, TD, and BlackRock Inc. flagged in the Teck Resources ethics complaint
Former CEO of BioteQ Environmental Technologies (appointed 2011), which had contracts with Teck Resources for selenium contamination treatment
Former CEO of QuestAir Technologies (gas purification company, from 2002)
Former Senior VP at Nexterra Systems (biomass company, from 2009)
Rhodes Scholar; degrees from University of Saskatchewan, Oxford University, and McGill University
Former consultant at Bain & Company and advisor to Saskatchewan Premier Roy Romanow (1991-1995)

key_votes.vote: Supported as Minister of Environment and Climate Change
Supported; stated Canada needs to extract full value from resources and use revenue to reduce emissions

profiles.name: Julie Dabrusin
cabinet_roles: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Canadian Heritage (2019-2021)
Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Environment and Climate Change and to the Minister of Energy and Natural Resources (2021-2025)
Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Nature (2025-present)
profiles.background: Canadian lawyer; raised in a Jewish household in Montreal; undergraduate degree in Near and Middle Eastern Studies from McGill University (1994); visited Israel twice (CEGEP kibbutz volunteer program and McGill archaeological dig)

controversies.title: No major ethics violations or scandals found in public record
controversies.summary: Web searches did not surface any ethics investigations, scandals, or formal complaints against Julie Dabrusin as of the research date.

lobbying_highlights.note: Listed in Canada's Lobbyists Registration System for communications particularly related to environmental and climate policy matters
As Parliamentary Secretary for Environment/Energy (2021-2025), was contacted by lobbyists on Mining, Environment, Climate, and Economic Development subjects
Promoted to Minister of Environment in 2025, making her a primary target for energy and environmental lobbyists

profiles.maid_position: Voted YES on both Bill C-14 (2016, legalizing MAID) and Bill C-7 (2020, expanding MAID eligibility). No public dissenting statements found; voted in line with Liberal Party position.

foreign_connections.note: Jewish heritage; raised in Montreal Jewish household
foreign_connections.detail: Identified as one of two Jewish MPs elevated in PM Carney's cabinet (alongside Evan Solomon). Described as positioned to shape policy on Canada-Israel relations.

foreign_connections.note: Published an August 2025 statement on Israel and Palestine on her official website
No CIJA-sponsored trips to Israel found in public records; her two known Israel visits predate her political career (CEGEP kibbutz program and McGill archaeological dig)

financial_notes.note: No financial controversies, improper expense claims, or gifts issues found in public record
Professional background as a lawyer before entering politics

key_votes.vote: Actively supported as Minister of Environment

profiles.name: Judy Sgro
cabinet_roles: Chair, Standing Committee on International Trade
Chair, Canadian House of Commons Liaison Committee (since 2016)

controversies.title: Strippergate (2004-2005)
controversies.summary: As Immigration Minister, accused of granting a special immigration permit to Alina Balaican, a Romanian who entered Canada to work as a stripper, and who was a campaign supporter. Her acting chief of staff Ihor Wons met with strip club owner and Liberal donor Terry Koumoudouros at the House of Lancaster strip club to discuss immigration cases. Over 30 Immigration employees were subpoenaed.
controversies.outcome: Ethics Commissioner Bernard Shapiro partially cleared Sgro in May 2005, finding she did not know her staffers had placed her in a conflict of interest. She resigned as Immigration Minister in January 2005.

controversies.title: Ottawa Condo Expense Scandal (2006-2015)
controversies.summary: Purchased an Ottawa condo for $138,000 in 2001, transferred title to her adult children in 2006, then claimed $22,000/year in rent paid to her children as parliamentary living expenses. This violated rules forbidding MPs from claiming expenses on goods or services contracted from family members.
controversies.outcome: Forced by the Board of Internal Economy to repay approximately $60,000 in improperly claimed living expenses.

controversies.title: 2017 Italy Trip — Conflicting Payment Stories
controversies.summary: Travelled to Matera, Basilicata region, Italy on an 'economic development' trip. The Basilicata Cultural Society of Canada's treasurer confirmed to the Toronto Star that the society paid for Sgro's travel. Sgro claimed she paid herself but declined to provide documentation. Under Canada's ethics code, all sponsored travel must be reported to the ethics commissioner.
controversies.outcome: Conservatives called for an ethics commissioner investigation in August 2021 during the federal election campaign.

lobbying_highlights.note: As Chair of Standing Committee on International Trade, positioned to receive trade-related lobbying
Focus areas as MP include immigration policy, housing, and international trade

profiles.maid_position: Voted YES on both Bill C-14 (2016) and Bill C-7 (2020). Expressed personal concerns about minors accessing MAID and about doctors being forced to participate against conscience. Advocated for emphasis on palliative care. Ultimately supported C-14 citing the Supreme Court's unanimous ruling that Canadians suffering intolerably have the right to request assistance.

foreign_connections.note: Member of the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC)
foreign_connections.detail: As an IPAC member, was targeted by APT31, a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group associated with the Hubei State Security Department in Wuhan, in a 2021 pixel reconnaissance cyberattack. Sgro demanded to know why Canadian MPs were not informed sooner about the targeting.

foreign_connections.note: Led a parliamentary delegation to Taiwan
foreign_connections.detail: Travelled to Taipei as part of the Canada-Taiwan Friendship Group. Trip was sponsored by the Taiwanese government (Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Canada). Benefits included approximately $500 in gifts, $6,809 in transportation, and $2,221 in accommodation.

foreign_connections.note: Accepted over $24,000 in total sponsored international travel (based on recent disclosure records)

financial_notes.note: $60,000 repaid to House of Commons for improperly claimed living expenses on family-owned Ottawa condo (2010-2015)
$22,000/year rent paid to her children for a condo she originally purchased for $138,000 and transferred to them
Conflicting stories about payment for 2017 Italy trip; declined to provide documentation
Over $24,000 in total sponsored international travel disclosed
Taiwan delegation travel: $6,809 transportation + $2,221 accommodation + $500 gifts, paid by Taipei Economic and Cultural Office
